_readme: 리스닝 문항 원본. tools/build_listening.py가 이 파일 하나로
audio/*.m4a 와 questions_listening.js 를 함께 생성한다.
turns[].t 안에서 쓸 수 있는 마크업 (그 외 문자는 전부 이스케이프됨):
turns[]의 style/rate/pitch 는 Azure SSML로 그대로 전달된다.
cast는 잠정값이다. 키 발급 후 voices/list로 각 음성의 실제 지원 스타일을
확인한 뒤 확정할 것. style을 지원하지 않는 음성에 style을 주면 무시된다.
_cast_note: 2026-08-09 voices/list로 확인 후 확정. 6개 배역 전부 스타일 지원 음성으로 통일했다.
en-US에 아동 남성 음성이 없어 student_m은 비교적 젊게 들리는 Jason으로 잡았고,
짝을 맞추려고 student_f도 아동 음성(Ana) 대신 Sara로 통일했다.
Ana는 진짜 아동 음성이지만 스타일을 전혀 지원하지 않아 prosody 문항에 못 쓴다.
그걸 쓰면 같은 '여학생'이 문항마다 다른 나이로 들리므로 일관성을 택했다.
Azure에 disgruntled 스타일은 없다. 비꼼은 unfriendly + 느린 속도 + 낮은 음높이로 근사한다.

announcer_f.note: 교내 방송 — 교사와 구분되게 별도 음성

announcer_m.note: 교내 방송 — 교사와 구분되게 별도 음성

turns.t: Minjun, I've been thinking about our science fair project.
The poster? I already picked the colors. Blue and green.
That's the thing. I don't think a poster is enough. Everyone does posters.
So we start over? It's due Friday.
Not start over. Same research. But we show it as a live demonstration, and grow the crystals right in front of the judges.
Okay. That would be hard to forget. Let's ask Ms. Park about bringing the equipment.

items.stem: What are the students mainly discussing?
choices: Which colors to use on their poster
Asking Ms. Park for more time
Changing the way they will present their project
Deciding what topic to research
items.explanation: 포스터 색·마감일·Ms. Park는 모두 언급되지만 곁가지다. 대화의 중심은 '같은 연구를 포스터가 아니라 실연으로 보여주자'는 발표 방식 변경이다.

turns.t: Ms. Reyes, do you have a minute? It's about band.
Of course. You're thinking of joining?
I was. But practice is every Tuesday and Thursday after school. That's when I have math tutoring.
Ah. So the question isn't whether you want to join. It's whether you can.
Right. And I don't want to give up tutoring. My grades just came back up.
Then let's not force it this semester. Try the spring auditions instead. Practice moves to mornings then.
Mornings I could do.

items.stem: What is the conversation mainly about?
choices: How the student improved his math grades
How to prepare for the spring auditions
A scheduling conflict that delays the student's plan
Why the student wants to stop his tutoring
items.explanation: 성적·오디션은 언급만 될 뿐이고, '과외를 그만두고 싶어한다'는 선택지는 오히려 반대다(그만두고 싶지 않다고 직접 말한다). 전체를 관통하는 것은 '하고 싶지만 시간이 겹쳐 이번 학기는 미룬다'는 일정 충돌이다.

turns.t: Did you finish the reading for history?
Chapter nine? Yeah. Took me two hours.
Two hours! It took me forty minutes.
Because you skip the primary sources. I read all the letters and the diary entries.
Those aren't on the test.
Maybe not. But last week Mr. Cho asked why the farmers moved west, and nobody could answer. It was in the letters.
Hm. Okay. Show me how you read them.

items.stem: What is the main point the boy makes?
choices: The extra sources explain things the chapter does not
The reading assignment is too long for one night
Mr. Cho asks questions that are unfair
The girl should spend two hours on homework
items.explanation: 두 시간·Mr. Cho의 질문은 근거로 든 세부사항이다. 소년의 요지는 '시험에 안 나오는 1차 자료에 교과서가 답하지 못하는 내용이 들어 있다'는 것.

turns.t: Good morning, students. A note about the library. Starting Monday, the second floor will be closed while new shelves are installed. The first floor stays open, and all the computers have been moved down there. If you have books due that week, don't worry. Nothing counts as late until the second floor reopens on the twentieth. Study rooms can still be booked at the front desk, but there are four now instead of nine, so book early. Thank you.

items.stem: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
choices: To remind students to return overdue books
To announce that the library will close completely
To introduce new computers on the first floor
To explain how library service changes during the work
items.explanation: 연체·컴퓨터·스터디룸은 모두 '공사 기간 중 이용 방법'의 하위 항목이다. '도서관이 완전히 닫힌다'는 1층은 계속 연다고 했으므로 사실과 다르고, 컴퓨터는 새것이 아니라 1층으로 옮겨진 것이다.

turns.t: Attention, seventh graders. You've heard that Field Day is Friday. Yes, it's still happening. But I need to talk about something else. Last year, forty-two water bottles, eleven jackets, and one pair of glasses were left on the field. We kept them a month. Almost nobody came. So this year, each homeroom gets a labeled bin at the edge of the field. Everything goes in your bin, not on the grass. At the end of the day your homeroom teacher carries the bin back inside. Field Day is the fun part. This is the part that decides whether you go home with your things.

items.stem: What is the announcement mainly about?
choices: A new system for keeping track of students' belongings
How many items students lost last year
Whether Field Day will take place on Friday
What homeroom teachers must do on Friday
items.explanation: Field Day 개최 여부는 첫 문장에서 언급하고 바로 넘어간다('하지만 다른 얘기를 하려고 한다'). 분실물 개수는 근거, 담임 역할은 세부 절차이고, 핵심은 새로 도입하는 물품 관리 방식이다.

turns.t: So. Octopus arms. Here's what surprised scientists. An octopus has about five hundred million nerve cells, close to a dog. But only a third of them are in its head. The rest are spread through the eight arms. What that means is strange. Each arm can taste, touch, and decide on its own. If an arm is separated from the body, and this has been tested, the arm will still reach for food and pull it toward where the mouth used to be. The octopus doesn't send an order to every arm. It gives a general goal, and the arms work out the details themselves.

items.stem: What is the talk mainly about?
choices: How many nerve cells an octopus has
How an octopus's arms act largely on their own
Why octopuses are as intelligent as dogs
How octopuses find and catch their food
items.explanation: 신경세포 수와 개 비교는 근거로 든 수치이고, 먹이를 잡는 이야기는 예시다. 전체 요지는 '팔 하나하나가 스스로 판단한다'는 것.

turns.t: When we talk about the invention of paper money, most people picture a government printing bills. That's not how it started. In China, about a thousand years ago, merchants traveling long distances got tired of carrying heavy strings of copper coins. So they left the coins with a trusted shop and took a written receipt instead. The receipt could be traded, and someone in another city would honor it. For almost two hundred years this was a private arrangement between merchants. No emperor involved. The government stepped in only later, once it noticed the paper was already circulating like money. So paper money wasn't handed down from above. It was invented from below, and then taken over.

items.stem: What is the speaker's main point?
choices: Paper money began among merchants before governments took it over
Copper coins were too heavy to carry on long journeys
Chinese merchants often traveled between distant cities
The Chinese government printed the first paper receipts
items.explanation: 동전의 무거움은 계기, 상인의 이동은 배경 설명이다. '정부가 최초의 지폐를 찍었다'는 정부가 나중에야 개입했다는 내용과 정반대다. 요지는 마지막 문장의 '위에서 내려온 게 아니라 아래에서 발명되어 나중에 접수되었다'이다.

turns.t: Two towns, same river, same year. Town A built a tall concrete wall along the bank. Town B bought the low fields beside the river and let them flood on purpose. They planted grass and put the playground on higher ground. Ten years later, a big storm came. Town A's wall held for six hours, and then the water came around the end of it, into streets that had been built lower and lower because people felt safe. Town B's fields filled up, the water spread out, and the town center stayed dry. Now, the wall wasn't badly built. The problem is what a wall teaches you. It tells you the water will never come, so you stop planning for the day it does.

items.stem: What is the speaker mainly arguing?
choices: Town B was simply luckier than Town A during the storm
Concrete walls are usually built too weak to hold
Towns should never be built beside a river
Flood defenses can create a false sense of safety
items.explanation: 'the wall wasn't badly built'이라고 직접 부정했으므로 '벽이 부실했다'는 오답이고, 마지막 두 문장이 요지다 — 벽은 '물은 오지 않는다'고 가르쳐서 대비를 멈추게 만든다. '운이 좋았다'가 아니라 구조적 문제를 말하고 있다.

turns.t: I didn't say she took the book.

items.stem: What does the speaker most likely mean?
choices: She may have taken something other than the book
Someone other than her may have taken the book
The speaker never mentioned the book at all
She borrowed the book rather than took it
items.transcriptMarked: I didn't say **SHE** took the book.  ← 'she'에 강세
items.explanation: 글자는 같아도 강세 위치가 뜻을 정한다. 'she'를 강조하면 '그 애가 가져갔다고는 안 했다' = 다른 사람일 수 있다는 뜻. 'book'을 강조했다면 '책이 아닌 다른 것을 가져갔다'가 답이 된다.

turns.t: I asked for the blue folder on my desk.

items.stem: What mistake is the speaker correcting?
choices: The wrong color folder was brought
The folder was taken from someone else's desk
The folder was not on a desk at all
More than one folder was brought
items.transcriptMarked: I asked for the blue folder on **MY** desk.  ← 'my'에 강세
items.explanation: 'my'에 강세가 놓였으므로 대조되는 것은 '내 책상 vs 다른 사람 책상'이다. 색깔이 문제였다면 'blue'에 강세가 왔을 것.

turns.t: They moved practice to six in the morning.
Oh, that's just great.

items.stem: How does the girl feel about the change?
choices: She is pleased that practice will be earlier
She is unhappy about the new time
She is surprised no one told her sooner
She thinks the new time is fair to everyone
items.transcriptMarked: Oh, that's just great.  ← 평탄하고 느린 내림조 = 비꼼
items.explanation: 단어만 보면 칭찬이지만 어조가 반대를 말한다. 느리고 낮게 깔리는 평탄한 억양은 영어에서 전형적인 비꼼(sarcasm) 신호다.

turns.t: Good news. I've put you in the front row for the concert.
Thank you. [p600] That's very kind.

items.stem: What does the boy's tone suggest?
choices: He did not hear which concert she meant
He is less pleased than his words suggest
He is genuinely delighted with the seat
He is confused about where to sit
items.transcriptMarked: Thank you. ⟨0.6초 휴지⟩ That's very kind.  ← 예의는 갖추되 가라앉은 어조
items.explanation: '감사합니다'라는 말과 달리 휴지와 가라앉은 억양이 반가움 없음을 드러낸다. 말의 내용과 어조가 어긋날 때는 어조 쪽이 진심이다.

turns.t: Can you have the report ready by tomorrow?
Well, [p500] I suppose [p320] I could try.

items.stem: How does the girl feel about the deadline?
choices: She is reluctant and not at all sure
She is confident she will finish in time
She has already finished the report
She did not understand the question
items.transcriptMarked: Well, ⟨0.5초⟩ I suppose ⟨0.32초⟩ I could try.  ← 휴지 + 느린 속도
items.explanation: '할 수 있다'가 아니라 '해 볼 수는 있을 것 같다'에 긴 휴지가 겹쳤다. 휴지와 채움말(well)은 내키지 않음·자신 없음의 신호다.

turns.t: Did you like my painting? Be honest.
[p900] It's really... interesting.

items.stem: What does the boy's pause suggest?
choices: He did not hear her question clearly
He is genuinely impressed by the painting
He wants her to ask the question again
He is looking for a polite way to avoid criticizing it
items.transcriptMarked: ⟨0.9초 침묵⟩ It's really... interesting.  ← 답 앞의 긴 침묵
items.explanation: 칭찬이 진심이면 즉시 나온다. 대답 앞의 긴 침묵과 'interesting' 앞의 머뭇거림은 부정적인 평가를 돌려 말하려는 신호다.

turns.t: You finished the whole thing?

choices: Expressing surprise and checking if it is true
Giving the listener an instruction
Complaining that the work took too long
Stating a fact she already knew
items.transcriptMarked: You finished the whole thing↗  ← 문장 끝이 올라감
items.explanation: 어순은 평서문이지만 끝을 올려 읽으면 놀람 섞인 확인 질문이 된다. 내려 읽었다면 이미 알고 있는 사실을 담담히 말하는 진술이 된다.

turns.t: For the project you'll need paper, scissors, glue...

items.stem: What does the speaker's intonation tell you?
choices: These three items are the only ones needed
The speaker is unsure the items are necessary
The list is not finished yet
The speaker is asking someone to bring the items
items.transcriptMarked: paper↗, scissors↗, glue↗  ← 마지막 항목도 올림조 = 목록 계속됨
items.explanation: 영어 목록에서 마지막 항목은 내림조로 끝나 완결을 알린다. 여기서는 'glue'까지 올림조라 항목이 더 남았다는 신호.
